body:
## Summary Split a GPU into two green-context streaming-multiprocessor partitions, give each partition its own CUDA stream, and have both streams issue all-reduces on the **same** SGLang custom all-reduce communicator. The custom all-reduce kernels wedge permanently: on every rank the kernels stay resident, the GPU pins at 100% utilization forever, and no collective ever completes. There is no error, no timeout, no recovery — a silent hang. The processes do not die on `SIGTERM` (the kernels are spin-waiting); only `SIGKILL` frees the GPUs. The failure needs **two custom all-reduce kernels of one communicator in flight at the same time**. It is not "green contexts are broken" and not "custom all-reduce under any concurrency": - the same two-partition workload with custom all-reduce disabled (NCCL carrying the all-reduces) runs clean; - custom all-reduce issued from **one** partition only, concurrently with ordinary compute — or with a second communicator's NCCL all-gather, or with a burst of 118 NCCL all-reduces — on the other partition, also runs clean; and - **two distinct custom all-reduce communicators**, one per partition, issued concurrently, run clean as well (220/220 iterations). Only sharing the communicator between the two in-flight all-reduces wedges (full table below). Found while using the green-context multiplexing substrate SGLang already exposes through `--enable-pdmux`: partition the GPU into two streaming- multiprocessor green contexts and run one CUDA stream per partition on an NVLink pair. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | sglang | 0.0.0.dev14693 (commit `2b1a30000`) | | sgl-kernel | 0.4.4 | | custom all-reduce | `CustomAllReduceV2` (the CUDA default: `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1`), one-shot push kernel | | torch | 2.11.0+cu130 | | NCCL | 2.28.9 | | CUDA | 13.0 | | Driver | 580.159.03 | | GPUs | 2× NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, NVLink pair (108 streaming multiprocessors, split 92/16) | | Transport | NVLink peer-to-peer (custom all-reduce active) | ## Reproduction Two processes, one per GPU. Each rank creates a large/small green-context stream pair with `sgl_kernel.spatial.create_greenctx_stream_by_value` (each stream confined to its streaming-multiprocessor partition) and one custom all-reduce communicator, built through SGLang's own `dispatch_custom_allreduce`, so the run exercises whatever the server would use (on CUDA: `CustomAllReduceV2`, the just-in-time one-shot push kernel). Every iteration issues one all-reduce on each partition stream. A 60-second watchdog turns the hang into a nonzero exit, because the spin-wait is not interruptible from Python. ``` python3 ca_v2_minimal_repro.py # -> permanent hang; watchdog exits 3 ```
ca_v2_minimal_repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Minimal reproducer: SGLang's custom all-reduce permanently deadlocks when two green-context streaming-multiprocessor partitions of one GPU issue all-reduces on the same communicator concurrently. Two ranks, one process per GPU, on an NVLink pair. Each rank splits its GPU into a large and a small green-context partition and issues an all-reduce on the SAME communicator from BOTH partition streams every iteration. The kernels wedge: both GPUs pin at 100% utilization forever, the kernels stay resident, and no collective completes. Nothing raises -- the watchdog below is the only thing that ends the run. The communicator is built through SGLang's own dispatch, so this exercises what the server uses (on CUDA: CustomAllReduceV2, the just-in-time one-shot push kernel `all_reduce_one_shot_push_kernel`). Run inside the container (needs sglang + sgl_kernel), on an NVLink GPU pair: python3 ca_v2_minimal_repro.py # -> deadlock, watchdog exits 3 GPUS=2,3 python3 ca_v2_minimal_repro.py # -> choose the GPU pair Exit code: 3 = deadlock reproduced; 0 = ran to completion; other = setup error. """ import os import sys import threading os.environ.setdefault("SGLANG_SKIP_P2P_CHECK", "1") os.environ.setdefault("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", os.environ.get("GPUS", "0,1")) import torch # noqa: E402 import torch.distributed as dist # noqa: E402 import torch.multiprocessing as mp # noqa: E402 WORLD = 2 SMALL_SM = 16 # small partition; the rest of the streaming multiprocessors go to the large one ITERS = 200 NUMEL = 64 * 1024 # 128 KB of bfloat16 -> the one-shot push path TIMEOUT_S = 60 def watchdog(rank): """The kernels spin-wait, so the hang is not interruptible from Python and SIGTERM does not free the GPU; a hard exit is the only reliable escape.""" def boom(): print(f"[rank{rank}] DEADLOCK: no progress for {TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s -- the " f"all-reduce kernels are resident and spinning.", flush=True) os._exit(3) t = threading.Timer(TIMEOUT_S, boom) t.daemon = True t.start() return t def worker(rank): os.environ.setdefault("MASTER_ADDR", "127.0.0.1") os.environ.setdefault("MASTER_PORT", "29591") torch.cuda.set_device(rank) device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}") dist.init_process_group("cpu:gloo,cuda:nccl", rank=rank, world_size=WORLD) group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo") # custom all-reduce needs a non-NCCL group from sgl_kernel.spatial import create_greenctx_stream_by_value, get_sm_available from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce import ( dispatch_custom_allreduce, ) total_sm = get_sm_available(rank) s_large, s_small = create_greenctx_stream_by_value( total_sm - SMALL_SM, SMALL_SM, rank ) comm = dispatch_custom_allreduce(group=group, device=device)( group=group, device=device ) assert not comm.disabled, "custom all-reduce is disabled (no NVLink peer access?)" if rank == 0: print(f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)} | {total_sm} streaming multiprocessors " f"split {total_sm - SMALL_SM}/{SMALL_SM} | {type(comm).__name__} | " f"{ITERS} iterations", flush=True) big = torch.ones(NUMEL, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16) small = torch.ones(NUMEL, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16) t = watchdog(rank) for _ in range(ITERS): # One all-reduce on each partition's stream, on the SAME communicator. with torch.cuda.stream(s_small): assert comm.custom_all_reduce(small) is not None with torch.cuda.stream(s_large): assert comm.custom_all_reduce(big) is not None torch.cuda.synchronize() # never returns once the kernels have wedged t.cancel() if rank == 0: print(f"[result] {ITERS} iterations completed -- no deadlock.", flush=True) comm.close() dist.destroy_process_group() def main(): if torch.cuda.device_count() < WORLD: sys.exit(f"need {WORLD} visible GPUs, have {torch.cuda.device_count()}") try: mp.spawn(worker, nprocs=WORLD, join=True) except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 -- ProcessExitedException on os._exit(3) if getattr(e, "exit_code", None) == 3: print("\n==== DEADLOCK REPRODUCED ====", flush=True) sys.exit(3) raise print("==== completed: no deadlock ====", flush=True) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
A fuller harness — with the passing NCCL control arm, the single-issue arms from the table below, CUDA-graph capture/replay, and `nvidia-smi` residency capture on the hang — is available on request. ## Observed behavior Permanent deadlock. Both ranks stop making progress and the final `torch.cuda.synchronize()` never returns. `nvidia-smi` during the hang, captured by the watchdog: ``` GPU 2: utilization 100 %, memory ~35 GiB, streaming-multiprocessor clock 1410 MHz GPU 3: utilization 100 %, memory ~35 GiB, streaming-multiprocessor clock 1410 MHz ``` Both GPUs pinned at 100% utilization indefinitely with the all-reduce kernels resident. Examining the wedged processes with `cuda-gdb` (user-triggered CUDA coredump) shows a resident `all_reduce_one_shot_push_kernel` pair — one per rank — stuck spin-polling their peer buffers with no forward progress. ## Where it is safe and where it is not All rows: 2× A100-SXM4-40GB NVLink pair, per-rank green-context split 92/16 of 108 streaming multiprocessors, identical two-stream concurrency. "Communicator A" and "communicator B" are two different communicators. | large partition (92) | small partition (16) | result | |---|---|---| | all-reduces, communicator A | compute only (matrix-multiply chain) | **520/520 iterations clean** | | all-reduces, communicator A | compute + one NCCL all-gather per iteration, communicator B | **520/520 iterations clean** | | all-reduces, communicator A | a burst of 118 NCCL all-reduces per iteration, communicator B | **220/220 iterations clean** | | all-reduces, communicator A | all-reduces, **communicator B** (a second, distinct custom all-reduce communicator) | **220/220 iterations clean** | | all-reduces, communicator A | all-reduces, **communicator A** | **wedged on the first concurrent iteration** | | NCCL all-reduce (custom all-reduce disabled) | NCCL all-reduce (custom all-reduce disabled) | **220/220 iterations clean** | The clean arms are not passing for lack of pressure: they carry 128 all-reduces of 1280 KB each per iteration on the large partition, and the two heaviest arms drive the small partition with either 118 NCCL all-reduces per iteration or a second, independent custom all-reduce. **Two distinct custom all-reduce communicators running concurrently, one per partition, are fine.** The boundary is therefore neither the amount of concurrency, nor the green context, nor custom all-reduce running opposite another collective: it is whether a second all-reduce of the **same communicator** is in flight. The wedge row reproduced 3/3 in the standalone harness and 1/1 as the positive control of the single-issue arms. The minimal reproducer above builds the communicator through `dispatch_custom_allreduce`, so the kernel it wedges is `CustomAllReduceV2` — the same path whose `all_reduce_one_shot_push_kernel` the coredumps named when this deadlocked a running server. (The green-context arm table was collected with the ahead-of-time `CustomAllreduce` class; both implementations keep the same kind of per-communicator, per-block synchronization state — see below.) ## Analysis The one-shot push kernel (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/distributed/custom_all_reduce_push.cuh`): - **Grid.** `num_blocks = m_max_num_cta_push` (line 209, commented "must be constant to ensure correctness"), and that value defaults to the **full device's** streaming-multiprocessor count — `props.multi_processor_count` (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/all_reduce.py:150,169-170`) — with 128 to 1024 threads per block (lines 210-215). The green context's budget does not enter into it. - **Rendezvous is per block index, across ranks.** Block `b` pushes its slice of the input into every peer's push buffer (`push_impl`, lines 108-128; peer targeting at line 182), then spins in `poll_impl` (lines 131-165) reading that same slice back out of its own buffer until every peer's copy has arrived. Arrival is encoded in the payload itself: positive zero is the "not yet here" sentinel, and the push side rewrites a genuine positive zero to negative zero (lines 66-71, 114-121). So block `b` of rank `r` cannot exit until block `b` of **every peer rank** has run its push phase. After consuming the data, the block writes the positive-zero sentinel back over the buffer (lines 158-163), which is what re-arms it for the next all-reduce. - **Two-stage epoch counter, per block, per communicator.** Which half of the push buffer an all-reduce uses comes from `PushController` (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/distributed/common.cuh:93-118`): `epoch()` reads `m_local_signal[blockIdx.x]` (line 101) and `exit()` advances it with a plain, non-atomic read-modify-write, `signal = (signal + 1) % kNumStages` (lines 111-114), with `kNumStages = 2` (line 96). That protocol is correct only if the all-reduces on one communicator are **totally ordered** — which is exactly what issuing them on a single stream provides. Two concurrent all-reduces on one communicator break it in two independent ways: 1. **Buffer aliasing.** Both kernels read the same epoch counter, so they land in the same half of the push buffer. One kernel's poll phase then overwrites, with the positive-zero sentinel, slices the other kernel's blocks are still waiting to see. The waiting block spins forever on data that has already been consumed. 2. **Epoch divergence.** The two `exit()` increments race (the update is not atomic), so a lost update can leave the two ranks' counters permanently out of step. One rank then polls the half of the buffer the other rank is not pushing into, and no amount of waiting fixes it. Neither condition is detectable from inside the kernel: the poll loop (lines 141-153) has no bound and no exit path. And a spinning block never retires, so it holds its streaming multiprocessor for the life of the process; on a green-context partition it holds part of that partition's whole budget, and since the grid is sized to the full device rather than to the partition, the blocks that have not been dispatched yet can never be scheduled either. Hence: 100% utilization forever, and immunity to `SIGTERM`. What is **not** the trigger, and is worth stating because it is the natural suspicion: one communicator issuing from one stream is fine *even though* its full-device-sized grid oversubscribes a smaller partition. Push and poll pair up per block index, and the two ranks' resident block sets are forced to overlap, so resident blocks always find their partner, retire, and free the partition for the rest of the grid. That is what the two clean single-issue arms above measure. The same hazard is present in the ahead-of-time implementation (`sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/custom_all_reduce.cuh`): `multi_gpu_barrier` (lines 192-225) keeps the same kind of per-communicator, per-block counters, increments `self_counter` with a non-atomic read-modify-write (line 204), and alternates between two peer-counter slots (lines 47-48, 207-208) on the same "one all-reduce in flight per communicator" assumption. The hang reproduces with that class too. ## Expected behavior Either the all-reduces complete under concurrent issue, or the implementation refuses to enter the fast path (or serializes the calls) instead of hanging. Failing that, the constraint should at least be documented and enforced: a custom all-reduce communicator supports only **one in-flight all-reduce at a time**, and issuing a second one concurrently is undefined behavior that currently manifests as an unkillable hang rather than an error. ## Severity - **Silent, permanent hang.** No exception, no NCCL or CUDA timeout, no recovery; the GPUs sit at 100% forever and the processes survive `SIGTERM`. - Custom all-reduce is **on by default** whenever NVLink peer access is available, so nothing unusual has to be opted into beyond issuing collectives from two streams — which is exactly what the green-context multiplexing that SGLang itself ships (`--enable-pdmux`) makes easy to do. - Nothing in the mechanism above depends on green contexts; any two concurrently executing streams sharing one communicator alias the same per-block state. We have measured only the green-context case. ## Workaround - `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (or `disabled = True` on the communicator) hands the all-reduces to NCCL and removes the deadlock, at a small latency cost on small messages. - Custom all-reduce remains usable when **only one** of the two partitions issues all-reduces on a given communicator: both single-issue arms in the table above ran 520/520 iterations clean, including the arm where the other partition drives a second communicator's NCCL all-gather every iteration. This is an empirical result on the hardware in the table, not a guarantee — nothing in the kernel enforces the single-issue rule, and a bounded-spin or occupancy check would be needed to make it one.

comments.body:
Two updates from working on a fix — both widen the scope of this report:

**1. Green contexts are not required.** The deadlock reproduces with two ordinary
`torch.cuda.Stream()`s issuing on the same communicator — no `sgl_kernel.spatial`,
no streaming-multiprocessor partitioning of any kind. The green-context setup in the
original reproducer is just where we happened to hit it. So the hazard is simply:
**one custom all-reduce communicator, two CUDA streams, concurrent issue.**

**2. The pull path deadlocks too.** The report named
`all_reduce_one_shot_push_kernel`, but `ONE_SHOT_PULL` wedges under the same
conditions (its `PullController::sync` spin loop). Both spin loops are unbounded.

Both are consistent with the mechanism described above: the protocol is
single-in-flight per communicator, and neither spin loop has a forward-progress
guarantee or a timeout.

A fix is validated and ready to submit: a host-side guard that serializes a
communicator across a stream change (fast path is a single stream-pointer compare;
zero cost under CUDA graphs, where no host call happens), plus a bounded spin in
both device loops that traps with a diagnostic instead of hanging forever — which
covers the case the host guard cannot see, two concurrent CUDA-graph replays.
Happy to open the pull request if that direction looks right to you.

title: [Bug] custom all-reduce (V2 one-shot push) deadlocks when one communicator is issued concurrently from two CUDA streams
